clearing_status.fact: SEC Release No. 34-102487 (Feb 25, 2025) granted a one-year extension to Dec 31, 2026 (cash) and Jun 30, 2027 (repo). As of Aug 2026, the SEC's own August 2026 Commissioner Uyeda statement (sec.gov) confirms deadlines are unchanged but multiple exemptive-relief requests remain pending: SIFMA inter-affiliate relief (published Apr 17, 2026, SEC Release No. 34-105262) and IIB non-U.S. transactions exemption, with combined comment period reopened and due Aug 31, 2026. No second deadline extension has been announced.
clearing_status.rationale: The rubric scores 1 for 'an official extension granted OR exemptive-relief requests pending' — both conditions are satisfied: the Feb 2025 one-year extension was formally granted, and multiple exemptive-relief requests (SIFMA, IIB) are actively pending as of Aug 2026. Score 2 requires a second formal extension or a missed deadline, neither of which has occurred.

plan_financing.fact: Japan 10-year JGB yield was ~2.78-2.85% in early August 2026 (CNBC, 2026-08-04; TradingEconomics, 2026-08-07), up from ~2.1% in March — a rise of roughly 60-75bps since fiscal concerns intensified. The May 2026 supplementary budget (~3 trillion yen) specified deficit-covering bonds while Takaichi pledged no net increase in total 2026 calendar-year issuance, but the funding path for the food tax cut (up to 5 trillion yen revenue loss) remains unspecified. Auctions are still clearing (5y bid-to-cover 3.10, Feb 2026; no failed auction reported), but the yield spike on fiscal news far exceeds the 25bps rubric threshold. Oxford Economics (Jun 12 2026) notes yields rose sharply from 2.1% to ~2.7% 'fuelled by market concern about Japan's more aggressive fiscal stance.'
plan_financing.rationale: The 10-year JGB yield is up roughly 60-75bps from pre-fiscal-concern levels and ~50bps on the fiscal news alone (May 2026 supplementary budget triggered a spike to 2.809% on May 20), placing it squarely above the 25bps UNCLEAR threshold; however, auctions are still clearing without a failed sale or emergency BOJ operation, ruling out a '2 = DISORDERLY' classification.

dissent.view: Some analysts argue the May yield spike (to 2.809%) and persistent elevation near 2.85% in August, combined with unresolved food-tax funding, could constitute near-disorderly conditions given the 40yr JGB breach of 4.2% in January 2026 (markets.financialcontent.com)

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings U.S. Private Credit Default Rate (PCDR, inclusive of distressed exchanges) remained at record high 6.0% TTM through May 2026 (LSTA/Fitch, published June 15 2026), and Bloomberg confirmed the TTM rate held at 6.0% at Q2-end (July 30 2026 Bloomberg report citing Fitch Q2 report).
direct_lending_default.rationale: The Fitch PCDR inclusive measure — the rubric anchor — has printed 6.0% for two consecutive months (April and May 2026) and held at 6.0% through end-Q2 per Fitch's own quarterly report; this is the most recent Fitch print and no subsequent Fitch update above or below 6.0% has been published, so 6.0% is retained per rubric.

dissent.view: Moody's estimates distressed restructurings accounted for ~65% of 2025 private credit defaults; excluding them produces headline rates of 1.6%-4.7%, materially below the Fitch inclusive measure
Proskauer Private Credit Default Index is count-based and typically runs 2-3 percentage points below Fitch PCDR inclusive measure
Morgan Stanley analysts warned of a potential spike toward 8% for the U.S. PCDR

redemption_gates.fact: In Q1 2026, at least five major private-credit/BDC funds triggered redemption caps in the same quarter: BlackRock HLEND ($26bn, 5% cap hit for first time, Bloomberg/cobaltintelligence Apr 2026), Blackstone BCRED ($82bn, raised cap to 7% and injected $400mn firm capital), Blue Owl OBDC II ($1.6bn, permanently closed/wound down), Blue Owl OCIC (~$34bn, capped at 5% on 21.9% requests), and Morgan Stanley North Haven Private Income (capped at 5% on 10.9% requests). In Q2 2026, Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Cliffwater, and Blue Owl (OCIC 18.8% request, $3.6bn) all gated for a second consecutive quarter (wildscrew.wordpress.com/cobaltintelligence, July 2026). Combined AUM of gated funds far exceeds $100bn.
redemption_gates.rationale: >=3 of the largest named funds triggered redemption caps/gates in Q1 2026, with combined AUM (BCRED $82bn + HLEND $26bn + OCIC $34bn alone = $142bn) far exceeding the $100bn rubric threshold; this pattern repeated in Q2 2026, firmly satisfying the WIDESPREAD criterion of level 2.

dissent.view: Some analysts (CAIA, iCapital, PGIM, April 2026) argue gates are functioning as contractually designed and do not reflect credit deterioration or systemic stress, framing this as a 'wrapper problem' not a systemic crisis — implying the severity classification may overstate systemic risk even if the count criterion is met.

new_imf_programs.fact: In the trailing 6 months (Feb–Aug 2026), the IMF Executive Board approved two new sovereign arrangements: (1) Ukraine EFF ~US$8.1bn approved 26 Feb 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/02/26/pr-26066-ukraine); (2) Mauritania ECF/EFF SDR 70.82mn approved 24 Jun 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/06/24/pr26223-mauritania). No sovereign missed-coupon or formal default event in this window was identified in authoritative sources.
new_imf_programs.rationale: Two newly approved IMF arrangements in the 6-month window (Ukraine, Mauritania) satisfy the RISING band definition of 1-2 new IMF arrangements; no missed coupons or standstills were found, and the total falls short of the >=3 threshold required for CLUSTER.

dissent.view: Ukraine's Feb 2026 EFF is a successor/renewal to the 2023 EFF rather than a first-time distress program, and Mauritania is a low-income country renewal; a strict 'new distress-driven' reading could place this closer to CALM (0) if rollovers are excluded.

china_ppi.fact: China PPI (industrial products, factory-gate) rose +3.5% year-on-year in July 2026, per NBS release dated 2026-08-09 (Xinhua: 'China's producer price index...went up 3.5 percent year on year in July, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) said Sunday'); MoM -0.7%.
china_ppi.rationale: The rubric scores on the SIZE of the signed move; +3.5% YoY is a moderate positive cost-push signal that exports input-cost pressure globally, driven by producer goods prices up +4.8% YoY, with the consumer-goods sub-index still soft - a meaningful but not extreme reading.

trade_actions.fact: At least 6 confirmed new major-economy trade measures vs China in the trailing 3 months: (1) US USTR new 12.5% Section 301 tariff on all Chinese goods (forced-labor basis), effective 24 Jul 2026 [China-Briefing/USTR, 23 Jul 2026]; (2) EU definitive anti-dumping duties 4.3-45.3% on Chinese car/lorry tyres, published 7 Jul 2026 [EC Trade, 9 Jul 2026]; (3) China MOFCOM adds 14 EU entities to export control list (dual-use ban), 24 Jul 2026 [USNews/AP]; (4) China MOFCOM bans trade with 7 US companies, tightens drone export controls to US, launches first foreign trade national-security investigation, 5 Aug 2026 [CNBC]; (5) EU Implementing Regulation 2026/843 revising AD duties on Chinese tinplate steel, 16 Apr 2026; (6) UK definitive anti-dumping measure on Chinese tin mill products, 12 Mar 2026.
trade_actions.rationale: Six or more discrete new major-economy trade measures are confirmed within 3 months, including a broad US Section 301 tariff round covering all Chinese imports (12.5% across all goods) - satisfying both the >=4 measures threshold AND the broad tariff round criterion (>=10% across a sector/all goods). This unambiguously maps to ESCALATING (value=2).

dissent.view: Some analysts note the 12.5% forced-labor tariff raises effective China rate by only 2.5% in practice (given stacking), and Xi-Trump September summit signals both sides are managing escalation rather than allowing a full breakdown - implying controlled escalation rather than unmanaged spiral.

license_flow.fact: As of August 2026, China's rare-earth magnet export licensing operates on a case-by-case basis with general licences issued only to three named producers (JL Mag, Zhong Ke San Huan, Yunsheng) since Dec 2025 and not broadly available; heavy-REE approvals (SmCo, Dy/Tb NdFeB) routinely take 60-120+ days; samarium, gadolinium and lutetium compounds were added to the 2026 licensing catalogue as newly controlled categories; NdPr alloy benchmark rose 21.4% through July 1, 2026; and Trump threatened 200% tariffs in August 2026 citing China's failure to supply magnets at agreed pace. Sources: blog.gettransport.com (Jul 2026), Arnold Magnetics/Duramag (Feb 2026), certivo.com (2026), china-briefing.com (Aug 2026 update), tech-insider.org (Jul 2026).
license_flow.rationale: The rubric requires score=1 when licensing is case-by-case or whitelist AND/OR processing time exceeds 30 days AND/OR a new category was added in the trailing 3 months — all three conditions are met simultaneously. Score=2 is not warranted because licences continue to be issued (no categorical denial or announced suspension), and price signals show constraint but not a complete freeze. [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (1 vs 0); held for review]

truce_status.fact: China's MOFCOM suspension of Oct-9-2025 rare earth export controls remains formally in force until Nov 10, 2026 (White House fact sheet, Nov 2025; China Briefing, Nov 10 2025), but on June 22, 2026 China added 10 US entities — including rare earth producers MP Materials and USA Rare Earth — to its export control list, prohibiting dual-use exports to those firms (Benchmark Minerals / Reuters / Morgan Lewis, June 22-25 2026). The April 2025 licensing regime was never suspended and exports remain ~50% below pre-control levels (EnkiAI/CSIS, May 2026).
truce_status.rationale: The formal truce instrument (MOFCOM suspension) has not been revoked, so the indicator is not a 2; however, the June 22 entity-list additions targeting the two largest US rare earth producers constitute an explicit 'partial breach' as defined in the rubric, and the truce is now within ~93 days of its Nov 10, 2026 nominal expiry with no confirmed renewal — squarely meeting the rubric's definition of 1 (EXPIRING/fraying).

re_blacklist.fact: China MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 (issued 22 June 2026) added 10 named US entities to its export-control list under the Export Control Law and Dual-Use Items Regulations, explicitly including MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc., alongside 8 defense/drone firms. Benchmark Minerals (25 Jun 2026) confirms: 'The measure is entity-specific rather than a blanket restriction on rare earth exports to the US.' Market signal: MP Materials share price was 'roughly flat' and USA Rare Earth 'modestly higher' on announcement day (Reuters via StockTitan), corroborating a firm-specific, not sector-wide, read.
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials and USA Rare Earth) are explicitly listed by MOFCOM as of 22 June 2026, satisfying rubric level 1 (entity-specific). Multiple sources — Benchmark Minerals, Arnold & Porter, StockTitan — confirm the restriction is firm-specific and not a categorical ban on the US rare-earth sector as a class, ruling out level 2.

hree_premium.fact: Dysprosium metal ex-China (Strategic Metals Invest retail, Aug 7 2026): $930.70/kg vs SMM China domestic $231.35/kg (Aug 3 2026), implying a multiple of ~4.5x; terbium ex-China $4,028.50/kg vs ~$1,095/kg China domestic (~3.7x). Benchmark Minerals (Mar 24 2026) reported 2025 dysprosium CIF North America at 4.4x EXW China.
hree_premium.rationale: Dividing the most recent ex-China retail price by the concurrent SMM domestic benchmark yields a ~4.5x multiple for dysprosium, the primary volume HREE; terbium shows a similar ~3.7x, giving a blended heavy-REE premium of roughly 4-5x consistent with the rubric.

genius_impl.fact: The statutory one-year deadline under Section 13 of the GENIUS Act (July 18, 2026) passed without any of the five primary federal regulators — OCC, FDIC, NCUA, Federal Reserve, or Treasury/FinCEN/OFAC — issuing final implementing rules; all 10 rule packages remained at the NPRM/proposed stage. Sources: Crypto Briefing (2026-07-18), CoinPaprika (2026-07-18), Crowdfund Insider (2026-07-19), CryptoNexa (2026-08-01), corroborated by OCC Federal Register NPRM (2026-03-02) and gncrypto.news (2026-07-18).
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric's level-2 criterion is 'deadline missed without final rules' — exactly what occurred on 2026-07-18 when all five agencies left their rulemakings at the proposal stage; no court stay or compliance-failure event is needed since the plain statutory deadline miss is itself the trigger. No corroborating funding-market stress signal (repo, SOFR-EFFR, MOVE) is required for a regulatory-status classification, and no such stress has been reported in connection with this miss.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Q2 2026: Combined hyperscaler capex tracking ~$740-760B for 2026, up ~77-84% YoY (Amazon raised to ~$220B, Google to $195-205B, Meta to $130-145B, Microsoft ~$120B+). Against this, Google Cloud accelerated from 63% to 82% YoY growth ($24.8B revenue); Azure crossed $100B ARR (up 41% FY2026); AWS AI hit a $25B+ run rate growing triple digits YoY. All four raised capex post-Q2 while AI-revenue growth accelerated QoQ. Sources: uncoveralpha.com (Q2 2026 earnings recap, ~Aug 2026); Statista (Aug 2026); tech-insider.org (Aug 2026); Meta Q2 2026 IR press release; bingx.com Q2 2026 earnings summary.
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Capex growth (~77-84% YoY) still substantially outpaces overall cloud revenue growth (~27-41%), satisfying the WIDE condition. However, AI-attributable revenue is accelerating QoQ across all major hyperscalers (Google Cloud 63%→82%, AWS AI tripling, Azure AI ~$40B+ ARR), and no hyperscaler cut its AI-revenue outlook, ruling out a score of 2 (WIDENING FAST).

dissent.view: Some analysts (Sequoia/David Cahn, Allianz Research) estimated a ~$600B annual gap between AI infrastructure spend and AI ecosystem revenue in 2025, with a capex-to-revenue divergence of ~46% exceeding the 2001 telecom overbuild peak of 32% — suggesting the gap may be structurally larger than Q2 results imply.

Microsoft Q2 FY2026 saw Azure miss expectations for the second consecutive quarter while capex surged 66% YoY to $37.5B, with one analyst noting 'capex is growing faster than expected and Azure a little bit slower' — a near-2 signal for Microsoft specifically.

gpu_refi_stress.fact: CoreWeave's 5-yr CDS spread hit ~855 bps on July 29, 2026, implying a 50% five-year default probability; simultaneously, the company's $2.6 billion leveraged loan facility was forced to reprice its spread 100-125 bps wider and accept maintenance covenants (1.35x DSCR, full amortization) before investors would commit. Bloomberg also reported (July 21, 2026) that ~80% of data-center securities sold since early 2025 now trade wider than at issuance, and Prime Data Centers paused a planned bond sale while Pure Data Centres Group scrapped a €1 billion bond. No confirmed default or distressed exchange has yet occurred. Sources: TechTimes/Bloomberg (July 29-Aug 3, 2026); Bloomberg Tax Distress Watch (July 21, 2026).
gpu_refi_stress.rationale: CoreWeave is a named GPU-backed borrower facing a concrete refinancing wall — its loan was actually repriced under investor pressure and now carries maintenance covenants — and its CDS prices distressed-level default odds, satisfying rubric level 1 ('a named borrower facing a refinancing wall' and 'banks offloading AI/data-center debt at a discount'). No confirmed default, distressed exchange, or failed refinancing has occurred, so level 2 is not yet warranted.

dissent.view: CoreWeave management stated on its Q1 2026 earnings call that 'we have no debt maturities until 2029 other than self-amortizing contract-backed debt and OEM vendor financing,' suggesting near-term liquidity is more manageable than CDS implies; and the company closed a $3.1B GPU-backed facility in the same period, showing lenders still willing to extend credit at scale.
CoreWeave's CDS blowout is characterized as company-specific and idiosyncratic, not a market-wide credit event, driven by its particular leverage and capex pace.

cmbs_office_delinq.fact: Trepp CMBS office delinquency rate hit an all-time high of 12.34% in January 2026, per Multi-Housing News reporting Trepp data (published ~early Feb 2026). The July 2026 overall Trepp rate rose to 7.86% with office among the rising sectors, but no sector-specific office % is available in open sources for July 2026.
cmbs_office_delinq.rationale: The rubric calls for the latest CMBS office delinquency rate as a percent; 12.34% is the most recent cleanly cited Trepp office-sector figure, anchored to hard delinquency data. July 2026 Trepp data confirms continued office stress but does not publish an open-source office-only rate, so 12.34% (Jan 2026) is the best available load-bearing number.

dissent.view: KBRA reports office CMBS delinquency rate rose 156 bps to 13.9% in January 2026 (KBRA-rated universe, which may differ from Trepp universe)
S&P Global headline states office rate 'surpasses 10.5%' in January 2026, lower than both Trepp and KBRA figures (paywalled, methodology may differ)

regional_bank_stress.fact: 4 US bank failures in 2026 per Forbes/American Banker (as of Jul 17, 2026): Metropolitan Capital Bank & Trust ($261M, Jan 30), Community Bank and Trust-West Georgia (May 1), Kentland Federal Savings and Loan ($3.7M, Jul 10), and Small Business Bank ($73M, Jul 17). Bisnow (Feb 2, 2026) found CRE/real-estate loan exposure as a contributing factor for Metropolitan Capital. The Federal Reserve issued an enforcement action against Small Business Bank citing 'significantly undercapitalized' status (American Banker, Jul 2026). No FDIC post-mortem formally attributes CRE concentration to the May or July failures; no failure exceeded $10bn; no coordinated interagency CRE emergency action found.
regional_bank_stress.rationale: The trailing 6 months contains 1-2 failures with at least partial CRE linkage (Metropolitan Capital is borderline on timing; no confirmed CRE nexus for the other three) plus at least one new public enforcement action (Fed vs. Small Business Bank), placing the indicator squarely in the ISOLATED band. The >=3 CRE-linked failures threshold for CLUSTER is not met given the absence of documented CRE as contributing factor for the May and July failures. [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (1 vs 0); held for review]

dissent.view: Bankrate (Feb 18, 2026) reported only 1 failure in 2026 at time of publication, likely reflecting a stale update; Forbes and American Banker confirm 4 failures by Jul 17, 2026

govt_stability.fact: PM Lecornu's minority government invoked Article 49.3 on 20-Jan-2026 to force the income side of the 2026 budget through the National Assembly without a vote; two subsequent no-confidence motions on 23-Jan-2026 (269 votes for LFI motion, short of 289 threshold) and two more on 02-Feb-2026 (260 votes LFI, 135 RN) all failed after Socialists and Republicans withheld support, allowing the 2026 budget to be formally adopted. Sources: Reuters/Al Jazeera/France 24/Euronews, 20-23 Jan and 02 Feb 2026.
govt_stability.rationale: Lecornu governs a minority/hung parliament with no working majority, required Article 49.3 to pass the budget, and has survived (not lost) multiple no-confidence votes — precisely the conditions of rubric band 1 (FRAGILE). No dissolution, no snap election, and no successful confidence vote has been recorded, so band 2 (COLLAPSE) is not met.

rating_action.fact: Fitch downgraded France from AA- to A+ (stable outlook) in September 2025 (Euronews/FXStreet, ~Sep 12-13 2025); S&P downgraded France from AA-/A-1+ to A+/A-1 with stable outlook on or around Oct 17 2025 (S&P Global Ratings article title confirmed); Moody's maintained Aa3 but moved to negative outlook Oct 25 2025. S&P reaffirmed A+ in May 2026 (Bloomberg, 2026-05-30). All three actions fall within the trailing 12 months to 2026-08-10.
rating_action.rationale: Two of the three major agencies (Fitch and S&P) executed actual one-notch rating cuts on France within the trailing 12 months, satisfying rubric band 2 (downgrade). Moody's added a negative outlook on Oct 25 2025, also within the window, but the executed cuts by Fitch and S&P are the load-bearing fact that drives the score to 2.

subprime_auto_dpd.fact: Fitch's subprime auto ABS 60-day delinquency index reached 6.11% in March 2026, down from a record 6.90% in January 2026 and 6.80% in February 2026, driven by seasonal tax-refund-related improvement — per Auto Remarketing citing Fitch Ratings Vehicle Depreciation Report (May 21, 2026). No later monthly Fitch figure (Apr–Jul 2026) has been publicly confirmed.
subprime_auto_dpd.rationale: The rubric calls for the latest reported subprime auto 60+ day delinquency rate as a percent; Fitch's March 2026 index reading of 6.11% is the most recent hard data point found, with Fitch explicitly warning the improvement is 'expected to be short-lived' as pressures persist through 2026. Confidence is medium because no April–July 2026 Fitch monthly print was retrievable, leaving a ~5-month gap to today (2026-08-10).

dissent.view: Motley Fool / Globe and Mail (July 2026) characterize the subprime 60+ day rate as 'around 6.8%' — this appears to reference the Jan-Feb 2026 peak, not the most recent monthly reading.
TradingEconomics (updated April 2026) shows 'Actual' = 6.80% (February 2026) as its most recent cell, predating the March 6.11% Fitch print cited by Auto Remarketing.

bnpl_delinq.fact: Affirm FQ3'26 SEC 8-K (May 7, 2026): 30+ day delinquency on monthly installment loans ex-Peloton/Pay-in-X = 2.8%, 'increased 29 basis points year over year'; allowance for credit losses = 6.0% of LHFI. Cohort ultimate net charge-offs tracking ~3.5% of GMV. CFPB/Richmond Fed (Mar 2026) report industry BNPL charge-off rate 1.83% in 2023, well below 3%. Klarna BNPL delinquency fell 15 bps YoY to 0.88% in Q2 2025.
bnpl_delinq.rationale: Affirm 30+ DPD rose ~29 bps YoY to 2.8% — up but below the 100 bps SPIKING threshold — and charge-offs remain contained at ~1.8-3.5% well under the 5% spike threshold, placing this squarely in the RISING (1) bucket. Klarna delinquency is declining YoY, so the rise is idiosyncratic to Affirm's longer-duration installment book rather than systemic.

dissent.view: Klarna BNPL global delinquency fell 15 bps YoY to 0.88% in Q2 2025, suggesting STABLE (0) at the pure-play BNPL end of the market

LendingTree March 2026 survey shows 47% of BNPL users paid late at least once in the past year (up from 41% in 2025 and 34% in 2024), a behavioral signal consistent with SPIKING stress, though not a formal 30+ DPD series

dollar_reserve_share.fact: The share of US dollar holdings in foreign exchange reserves increased to 57.13 percent in 2026Q1, from 56.42 percent in 2025Q4. Source: IMF Data Brief, data.imf.org/en/news/imf%20data%20brief%20july%201, published July 1, 2026.
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The IMF COFER July 2026 release is the primary authoritative source; the 57.13% figure is the most recent officially published USD share of total global FX reserves for 2026Q1, mapping directly to the rubric's request for the latest percent.

dissent.view: coferdata.com displays USD at 56.77% (with a -0.15pp change indicator), suggesting a possible Q2 2026 estimate or a display lag/rounding difference from the official 57.13% Q1 2026 figure

weaponization_event.fact: No new sovereign reserve seizure/confiscation executed in 2026: EU converted its Russian asset freeze to indefinite status on 11 Dec 2025 (procedural tightening, not new confiscation; EU chose a 'reparations loan' over outright seizure per IAI/globalsecurity.org, Apr 2026). BRICS Pay pilot launch targeted end-2026 at India BRICS Summit; Russian Deputy FM Ryabkov pegs full operational status to 2030; BRICS Pay own site states system 'remains in planning and early-pilot stage' as of mid-2025 (bricspayment.ru). BRICS Unit 100-unit pilot launched Oct 2025.
weaponization_event.rationale: The rubric requires either a new sovereign reserve seizure (none executed in 2026) or a major economy operationally moving reserve settlement off USD (BRICS Pay not yet operational) for a score of 2. What exists is official BRICS non-dollar settlement launches/pilots and rhetoric — squarely rubric band 1 (TALK/early launch, no operational shift).

dissent.view: Some sources (watcher.guru, informedclearly.com) characterise BRICS Pay as already 'live' and 'operational' in 2026 with 67% intra-bloc local currency trade, which could push toward band 2; however these appear to be advocacy/non-primary sources and contradict BRICS Pay's own site and BIS-linked data.

EU's Dec 2025 shift to indefinite freeze of €210bn Russian assets could be characterised as a materially new action (not just talk); Brookings/CFR note EU still has not executed confiscation and opted for loan structure.

insurer_exits.fact: NAIC MCAS report (Aug 5, 2026) documents company-initiated non-renewal rates up 96%-216% across ALL four U.S. geographic regions 2018-2024; named states with active non-renewal waves / market exits include at minimum CA, FL, LA, TX, CO, GA, OK (7+ states, one source enumerates 13). AM Best upgraded national HO segment outlook to stable (Dec 2025) but CA and FL state-segment outlooks remain materially weaker. Source: content.naic.org, Aug 5 2026; AM Best via leadgen-economy.com, Jun 25 2026.
insurer_exits.rationale: Non-renewal stress is confirmed across 7-13+ states (above the 5-state RISING threshold) but AM Best moved national outlook to stable and no top-10 insurer has fully exited a major state market in 2026, precluding level 2. The pattern fits RISING: elevated across 5-15 states with some markets (FL Citizens depopulation, softening reinsurance) stabilizing.

dissent.view: Climate Cosmos (Jun 2026) enumerates 13 specific states with active non-renewal/drop waves, which would be near the upper bound of RISING but not yet >15 states required for ACCELERATING.

insurance.com May 2026 survey shows only 7% of homeowners reported a cancellation/non-renewal and rates of carrier market exits are each ~2-3% of respondents, suggesting idiosyncratic rather than systemic scale from a consumer-demand perspective.

cat_losses.fact: Global H1 2026 insured nat-cat losses: Gallagher Re $46bn (28% BELOW 10-year average of $64bn); Munich Re $44bn (below 10-year H1 avg of $50bn); Aon $47bn (below 21st-century avg). Five consecutive quarters with no single event exceeding $10bn insured. Sources: Gallagher Re Natural Catastrophe and Climate Report H1 2026 (c. July 2026); Munich Re nat-cat H1 2026 press release July 30 2026 (munichre.com); Aon Global Catastrophe Recap H1 2026 July 22 2026 (aon.com).
cat_losses.rationale: YTD insured losses are 28-40% BELOW the 10-year average depending on source, and no single event has crossed $10bn, satisfying every condition for NORMAL (0). Neither the ELEVATED nor SEVERE thresholds are approached.

ss_reform_news.fact: 2026 SSA Trustees Report (ssa.gov/oact, issued 2026-06-09) projects OASI trust fund depletion in Q4 2032 -- one quarter earlier than 2025 report -- with 78% of benefits payable at depletion; 75-year actuarial deficit widened to 4.42% of taxable payroll from 3.82%. The PROMISE Act (S.4979) and Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act (H.R.9187) introduced but not enacted; Senate Finance Committee hearing held 2026-08-05. No automatic cuts triggered; no cuts enacted.
ss_reform_news.rationale: The 2026 trustees report materially worsened the depletion date and long-term shortfall, and bipartisan reform legislation is actively debated in Congress, matching rubric band 1 (DEBATE). No automatic reduction has been triggered (depletion has not occurred) and no legislation enacting cuts has been signed into law, ruling out band 2.

dissent.view: AARP (July 2026) opposes fast-track reform proposals, complicating enactment prospects, but this does not change the factual classification -- it reinforces that reform remains debate-stage, not enacted.

pension_leverage_event.fact: TPR's September 2025 Market Oversight report (thepensionsregulator.gov.uk) found that the LDI sector has made 'significant steps to improve resilience': the LDI market has halved to ~£0.7 trillion by March 2025, rate buffers have risen to ~300 bps (vs ~150 bps pre-Oct 2022), daily volatility in leveraged LDI assets is more than 50% lower than end-2021, and 'LDI arrangements remained resilient in January 2025 when gilt yields increased during a period of higher volatility.' No margin-call episode, forced gilt selling or central-bank intervention has been reported in 2026.
pension_leverage_event.rationale: TPR's own market-oversight report and monitoring data through early 2025 show buffers well above the 250 bps regulatory minimum and no forced selling or intervention episode, matching rubric band 0 (buffers adequate, no margin stress). The absence of any 2026 regulator flag, FT/Reuters episode report, or BoE intervention announcement means no upgrade to band 1 or 2 is warranted.

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI): funded ratio of the 100 largest U.S. public pension plans was 88.7% as of June 30, 2026, down from 89.1% as of May 31, 2026 (Milliman PPFI July 2026 release, published July 30, 2026; https://www.milliman.com/en/insight/public-pension-funding-index-july-2026).
funded_ratio.rationale: The Milliman PPFI is the preferred primary source per the rubric and its June 30, 2026 reading of 88.7% is the most recent published data point; the rubric calls for reporting a representative large US public-pension funded ratio as a percent, and 88.7 maps directly to that instruction. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-06-30 data but the prior applied value was FY2026 (as of 2026-07-23) data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: Equable Institute 'State of Pensions 2026' projects the national funded ratio for 253 statewide and municipal systems at 85.0% for FY2026 (up from 81.2% in 2025); this broader universe and accrual-based methodology yields a lower figure than Milliman's market-value PPFI.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition (emp.lbl.gov/queues, PDF published June 2026, data through end of 2025): 'the median duration from IR to COD was over 5 years for projects built in 2025'; separately, 'the median duration from submitting a request to signing an IA was well over 3 years in 2025' (LBNL press release, July 1 2026). Over 5 years = >60 months.
interconnection_months.rationale: The rubric asks for the latest LBNL median wait in months; LBNL reports IR-to-COD median as 'over 5 years' (>60 months) for the 2025 cohort, so 60 is the confirmed floor — consistent with the 2024 edition's exact 5-year (60-month) median for 2023 projects, with the 2025 figure meeting or exceeding that level.

dissent.view: LBNL Queued Up 2025 Edition (data through end of 2024) reported median IR-to-COD as 'over 4 years' for the 2018-2024 cohort broadly, implying ~48-54 months for that blended group — a lower figure than the 2025 single-year cohort result

dc_moratoria.fact: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed Executive Order No. 62 on July 14, 2026, establishing the nation's first statewide moratorium on new hyperscale data centers (50 MW+), immediately pausing DEC environmental permits for up to one year. Source: governor.ny.gov, July 14 2026. Additionally, DLA Piper (July 1 2026) reports 'more than 100 local moratoria have been adopted nationwide' and 'at least 12 states have considered moratorium legislation'; Maine's legislature passed a moratorium (vetoed); Georgia, Indiana counties, and Monterey Park CA also enacted local pauses/bans.
dc_moratoria.rationale: A statewide moratorium is now confirmed-enacted in New York (executive order in force since July 14 2026), directly satisfying the rubric's level-2 trigger of 'a statewide moratorium enacted.' More than 10 local jurisdictions have also adopted enacted pauses, further satisfying the '>10 jurisdictions' alternative threshold. Jurisdictions with enacted pauses/bans include: New York (statewide EO), Monterey Park CA (permanent ban), multiple Georgia counties (DeKalb etc.), multiple Indiana counties (Fulton and at least 3 others), Hill County TX (briefly enacted then rescinded), Howell Township/Sterling Heights/Pontiac MI, St. Charles MO, and dozens more per DLA Piper's count of 100+ local moratoria.

dissent.view: Maine's legislature passed a moratorium in April 2026 but Gov. Janet Mills vetoed it, so Maine does not count as enacted; some sources written before July 14 treat NY as still pending governor action.
Texas Hill County enacted a one-year moratorium in May 2026 but rescinded it June 4, 2026 after developer lawsuit, so it no longer counts as active.

ai_power_pressure.fact: The DOE invoked Section 202(c) emergency authority three times in 2026 within PJM to authorize curtailment of data centers with backup generation (most recently July 4, 2026); ERCOT suspended its Batch Zero Large Load classification process on Aug 3-7, 2026 and will seek a good-cause exception at the Aug 20 PUCT meeting; and New York Governor Hochul issued Executive Order No. 62 on July 14, 2026 imposing a statewide moratorium on new data center development -- all confirmed by Utility Dive (May 19 & July 4, 2026), Troutman Pepper Locke (Aug 4, 2026), and Sheppard (July 2026). IEA Electricity 2026 independently confirms 'over 2,500 GW of projects stalled in grid queues worldwide' and 'rising congestion-related curtailment.' LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition reports ~8,200 active U.S. projects (1,312 GW generation + 749 GW storage) as of end-2025.
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Confirmed forced curtailment of data-center load under three DOE Section 202(c) emergency orders within PJM, a statewide construction moratorium in New York, and ERCOT suspending large-load interconnection notifications all satisfy the rubric's Level 2 threshold of 'confirmed curtailment of data-center load, a declared grid emergency, or a power-scarcity-driven moratorium.' Physical evidence is corroborated by IEA and LBNL primary sources.

dissent.view: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition notes a 10% decrease in total active queue volume vs prior year, suggesting some easing at the margin of new project filings, not curtailment pressure on existing load.

FERC June 18, 2026 orders to all six RTOs aim to shorten interconnection queues, suggesting regulatory intent to ease the bottleneck -- but the backlog and curtailment events precede any queue-shortening impact.

mine_disruptions.fact: As of Aug 2026: (1) Grasberg (world #2, Indonesia) still operating at ~35% below pre-incident levels, targeting only 65% capacity H2 2026 per Freeport May 2026 earnings (mining.com, 2026-05-08); (2) Kamoa-Kakula (DRC, top-5) guidance cut to 290k-330kt vs 420kt target, Q2 output 64,328t with smelter at 60% capacity (Ivanhoe Mines press release, 2026-07-08); (3) Lundin Caserones suspended since 2026-07-18; Codelco Andina+El Teniente surface halted; Antofagasta Los Pelambres halted -- all due to Chile winter storms (mining.com, CNBC, ~2026-07-31). Benchmark Minerals and Goldman Sachs both forecast a 2026 copper market deficit driven by these cumulative disruptions.
mine_disruptions.rationale: Five top-20 mines have confirmed active production cuts/outages simultaneously (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, Caserones, Codelco Andina/El Teniente, Los Pelambres), well exceeding the >=3 threshold; multiple institutions explicitly forecast a market deficit -- squarely meeting the CLUSTER (2) rubric.

dissent.view: Some Chile storm disruptions described as temporary/precautionary (surface-only suspensions), not full mine outages, and Lundin maintained full-year guidance; Chilean disruptions may resolve within weeks -- reducing net permanent output loss
Startupfortune characterises Chilean storm impact as temporary, not catastrophic, noting 'immediate disruption looks temporary, not catastrophic'

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG April 2026 Lisbon meeting: projecting a 96,000 ton market surplus in 2026, reversing a previous forecast of a deficit of 150,000t, due to slower demand growth and increased secondary production. Source: ADMIS/ICSG, April 24 2026 (https://www.admis.com/icsg-flips-copper-forecast/).
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: A 96,000t surplus exceeds the +100kt threshold in the rubric, placing it in the SURPLUS band (0). The April 2026 ICSG revision is the most recent official ICSG number available.

dissent.view: ICSG October 2025 forecast: 150,000t refined deficit for 2026 - would score 2 (DEFICIT)
J.P. Morgan forecast: ~330,000t refined deficit for 2026 - would score 2 (DEFICIT)
Goldman Sachs reportedly forecast ~300,000t surplus for 2026 - would score 0 (SURPLUS)
Morgan Stanley cited ~590,000t deficit as 'most severe in 20 years' - would score 2 (DEFICIT)

drought_chip_farm.fact: Arizona Dept. of Water Resources reports D3 (Extreme) and D4 (Exceptional) long-term drought in every Arizona county as of the USDM August 4, 2026 release; Lake Mead fell to 1,040.5 ft on August 7, 2026, described as the lowest level ever recorded (western-water.com, citing USDM August 4 2026; azwater.gov).
drought_chip_farm.rationale: Confirmed D3/D4 classification across the entire state of Arizona satisfies the rubric's ACUTE threshold; Lake Mead at an all-time record low constitutes a corroborating confirmed physical infrastructure impact. No Taiwan 2026 fab curtailment found, but US Southwest D3-D4 alone is sufficient.

dissent.view: Southwest monsoon in July-Aug 2026 is delivering above-average seasonal rainfall to AZ/NM, improving short-term drought conditions even as long-term D3-D4 persists (drought.gov June 18 2026 monsoon update)

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation ~1,040.4 ft, storage ~7.02–7.45M AF = 26.9–28.5% of 26.12M AF capacity, per USBR daily gauge data (reservoirbench.com citing USBR, Aug 5 2026; coloradorivermonitor.com Aug 9 2026; Fortune/AP citing federal data Aug 8 2026). The lake is at or near its all-time record low since filling.
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 26.9–28.5% of capacity, Lake Mead is firmly below the rubric's 30% CRITICAL threshold. Additionally, at ~1,040 ft the reservoir is already ~10 ft below Hoover Dam's minimum power pool of 1,050 ft — a confirmed physical impact (reduced hydro generation capacity), not merely a forecast.

dissent.view: Colorado River Monitor (Aug 9 2026) reports 28.5% capacity vs reservoirbench/USBR showing 26.9% as of Aug 5 — minor discrepancy likely due to date difference and rounding, both below 30%.

water_dispute.fact: India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) 'in abeyance' after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack, confirmed suspended as of June 5 2026 (India MFA); India physically stanched flow through Baglihar Dam on the Chenab River (May 2025, Doordarshan/Newsonair); Pakistan has complained of 'abnormal, abrupt flow variations on the Chenab' in letters sent twice in 2025 and once in May 2026 (CNBC, June 22 2026); India's water minister declared Pakistan will receive 'not a single drop' and Pakistan's defence minister warned 'we will go to war' over water — though he added current events do not yet warrant military action (CNBC, June 22 2026); Pakistan raised the matter at the UN Security Council on July 24 2026 warning against 'weaponisation of water' (Nation.com.pk, July 24 2026).
water_dispute.rationale: A confirmed physical flow manipulation (Baglihar Dam stoppage) has already occurred, satisfying the rubric's 'deliberate flow cut-off carried out' criterion; separately, a formal war threat tied directly to the river/dam was made by Pakistan's defence minister, meeting the 'war threat tied to a dam/river' criterion — both independently qualify for level 2. The Indus dispute is therefore the dominant signal.

dissent.view: CSIS (May 2025) and Verisk Maplecroft (June 2026) note that India currently lacks full infrastructure to block Indus flows entirely, and that actual net flows remain broadly unchanged despite the Baglihar manipulation; they characterise the situation as coercive rhetoric with limited physical impact to date, implying a reading closer to level 1.

On the GERD/Nile front, analysts (pppescp.com, March 2026; Chatham House, April 2026) characterise that dispute as high-tension but diplomatically managed, with Trump offering mediation in January 2026 — consistent with level 1 rather than level 2.

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 131.1 points in July 2026, up 0.6% (0.7 points) from June 2026 (130.3) and up 1.0% YoY — highest reading since January 2023. Source: FAO official press release, fao.org/newsroom, released 7 August 2026.
fao_food_trend.rationale: Index is rising both MoM (+0.6%) and YoY (+1.0%), so rubric band 0 (FALLING) is excluded; MoM gain of 0.6% is well below the 5% SPIKING threshold and the 3-month rise (May 130.8 → June 130.3 → July 131.1) is roughly +0.2% over three months, far below the 10% SPIKING threshold — placing this squarely in band 1 (ELEVATED).

china_export_curbs.fact: NDRC officials stated in December 2025 that China would halt phosphate fertilizer exports through August 2026 (S&P Global/Platts, Dec 11 2025). On ~March 14-19 2026 Beijing further instructed exporters to immediately suspend nitrogen-potassium blends and additional phosphate varieties (Global Trade Alert, Mar 14 2026; Mysteel/OilChem Mar 26 2026 'zero-export' mandate effective Mar 19). As of July 29 2026 Fertilizer Daily confirmed China extended phosphate export curbs 'at least through August 2026,' with 50-80% of Chinese fertilizer export volumes restricted per Reuters/customs data. Food Security Portal (last updated ~Aug 2026) confirms China 'continues to maintain restrictions on fertilizer exports including urea and phosphate.' International urea prices rose ~40% from pre-war levels confirming physical price impact.
china_export_curbs.rationale: The March 2026 additions (NK blends, broader phosphate/zero-export mandate) represent a NEW and broadened restriction layered on top of the December 2025 NDRC phosphate suspension, satisfying rubric level 2 (tightened: new or broadened restriction in trailing 3 months, covering added products). The 40% urea price spike and 50-80% volume restriction provide confirmed physical/price corroboration beyond a forecast alone.

dissent.view: Philippines reportedly indicated China said fertilizer exports 'would not be restricted,' though Chinese officials never publicly confirmed this position

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: PortWatch recorded 2 transits on 2026-08-02 vs. ~73/day baseline; Reuters reported only 33 vessels Monday-Thursday Aug 4-7; sulfur loadings from Ras Laffan down ~55% vs. 2025; WTO confirmed fertilizer shipments through Hormuz 'came to a standstill'; Iran-Oman talks ongoing but Iran warned reopening not imminent; Brent at ~$84/bbl (~26% YoY) but well below the $100+ July peak. Sources: straits.live Aug 9 2026, Reuters Aug 7 2026, WTO blog Jul 10 2026, Lloyd's List via auronexgroup May 2026, TradingEconomics Aug 10 2026.
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: The strait is severely disrupted — fertilizer/sulfur/ammonia flows are at 3-5% of normal and costs/insurance are extreme — but vessels are still sporadically transiting and Iran-Oman diplomatic talks are active, satisfying the rubric's DISRUPTED (1) definition. Brent at ~$84 is elevated but has retreated sharply from the $100+ July crisis peak, and the rubric explicitly caps rating at 1 when convoys are still moving and talks are ongoing, even if volumes are far below normal.

dissent.view: straits.live and the Wikipedia 2026 Hormuz crisis article characterise the strait as 'effectively closed' to commercial shipping, which could support a rating of 2
Brent crude peaked above $100/bbl in late July 2026, which at that point would have corroborated a rating of 2, but has since retreated to ~$83-84 as of Aug 10

taiwan_tension.fact: China conducted two days of live-fire drills in the Taiwan Strait on 23–24 July 2026, near Dongshan Island off Fujian province; Taiwan's Defense Ministry detected 19 PLA aircraft (J-10, J-16, H-6 bombers, KJ-500 AEW) plus naval vessels, with 12 aircraft crossing the median line or its extension. Firing zones were within ~12 km of China's coastline, well short of Taiwan's territorial waters. (Sources: SCMP 23 Jul 2026; ASPI State of the Strait 21–28 Jul 2026; Epoch Times 23 Jul 2026). A separate Heritage Foundation/Daily Signal analysis dated 31 Jul 2026 characterised 2026 overall as a 'relative lull' in coercive PLA activity compared with 2025.
taiwan_tension.rationale: The July 23–24 live-fire drills with median-line crossings and named aircraft types constitute assertive, large-scale PLA activity—matching Rubric 1 (elevated). All firing zones stayed hugging China's coast with no blockade, no kinetic clash against Taiwan, and no full mobilisation, ruling out Rubric 2.

dissent.view: Heritage Foundation/Daily Signal (31 Jul 2026) frames 2026 as a 'relative lull' in coercive PLA activity, implying activity is closer to routine (Rubric 0) on a multi-month basis, driven by US-China diplomatic détente and PLA purges.

export_controls.fact: Within the trailing 3 months: (1) BIS opened a 2026 enforcement surge targeting chip exports to China (Kharon, June 2026); US MATCH Act advanced to ban DUV immersion lithography exports to China (April-July 2026); US Commerce Secretary Lutnick held private meetings with ASML over suspected EUV diversion (Asia Times, July 2026). ASML China sales volume fell 36%->19% QoQ confirming real restriction effect. (2) China MOFCOM on 22 June 2026 barred China-origin dual-use exports to 10 US firms incl. MP Materials (MOFCOM Announcement, riotimesonline/tech-insider citing MOFCOM); on 24 July 2026 extended to 14 EU firms; MOFCOM Announcement No.26 enforcement mechanism took effect 1 July 2026 (tech-insider.org, ~26 Jul 2026).
export_controls.rationale: Both the Western/allied side (BIS enforcement escalation, MATCH Act DUV legislation, ASML EUV diversion pressure) and the Chinese side (MOFCOM entity-specific export bans on US and EU companies, new enforcement mechanism No.26) have enacted distinct new measures within the trailing 3 months, satisfying the rubric's level-2 RETALIATION threshold: target country has enacted countermeasures in documented response to US/allied controls.

dissent.view: East Asia Forum (March 2026) argued the US has 'traded loud escalation for quiet enforcement' and Commerce was 'unlikely to proactively introduce new export control rules' in 2026 amid trade negotiations, suggesting the tightening is enforcement-only rather than new rulemaking — which would weight toward level 1 rather than 2.

fab_concentration.fact: As of H1 2026, TSMC runs ~150,000 wafers/month at 3nm and ~50,000-60,000 wafers/month at 2nm — all in Taiwan (Tainan Fab 18, Hsinchu Fab 20, Kaohsiung Fab 22). The Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 (3nm) completed construction in April 2026 and began equipment installation in Q3 2026, with volume production targeted for H2 2027. Japan Kumamoto Phase 2 (3nm) targets 2028. Zero ≤3nm wafer starts exist outside Taiwan today. Sources: TrendForce (Aug 3, 2026); Blackridge Research (2026); TrendForce Q1 2026 earnings summary (Apr 16, 2026).
fab_concentration.rationale: All operational ≤3nm capacity (~200,000+ combined monthly wafer starts) is located exclusively in Taiwan; overseas ≤3nm fabs are in equipment-installation or planning phases only, placing the outside-Taiwan share firmly at <10% (effectively 0%). This maps mechanically to rubric level 2 (EXTREME).

dissent.view: Nikkei/Trendforce (Dec 2025) reported TSMC projects ~30% of most advanced chips manufactured in the US once the full $165B Arizona build-out is complete (5 fabs); this is a future-state projection for ~2030, not current capacity, and does not alter the 2026 snapshot.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: PortWatch/JMIC recorded 2 commercial transits of the Strait of Hormuz on 2026-08-02 vs. a pre-crisis baseline of ~73/day (straits.live, 2026-08-09); Bab el-Mandeb weekly transits fell to 266-269 vs. 354 pre-blockade (Lloyd's List Intelligence, 2026-08-06); Brent crude is ~$84/bbl on 2026-08-10, well below the $120.88 April 2026 peak (TradingEconomics, 2026-08-10); Iran-Oman talks on a Hormuz shipping corridor were reported as 'nearing an agreement' as of the weekend of 2026-08-09 (TradingEconomics/Reuters).
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Both straits are severely contested — Hormuz transit near zero with active IRGC attacks and US naval escort/blockade, Red Sea down ~40% with live Houthi strikes on Saudi tankers — but Brent at ~$84 (off 30% from the $120 April peak) does not corroborate a sustained full-closure price signal, and ongoing Iran-Oman diplomatic talks plus US convoy operations cap the rating at 1 (CONTESTED) per rubric.

dissent.view: Hormuz 'effectively closed to commercial shipping' as of 2026-08-09, citing 2 transits vs. ~73/day baseline
Strait of Hormuz 'effectively closed to routine commercial shipping as of 30 July 2026' with major carriers having suspended transits

cable_incidents.fact: Windward Q2 2026 Undersea Cables Risk Report (published ~Aug 2026) documents 34,081 vessel proximity events and ongoing Baltic/Hormuz surveillance threats; UK Defence Secretary disclosed April 9 2026 that Russian submarines conducted covert surveillance over UK cables; Tasnim (May 11 2026) warned of potential Hormuz cable damage; Taiwan Matsu No.3 cable cut late April 2026 impacting 1,500 residents with backup activated. No authoritative source (Reuters, Cloudflare, Lloyd's List, official government notice) confirms a major cable currently severed and unrepaired causing significant connectivity loss as of Aug 2026. Sources: windward.ai/knowledge-base/q2-2026-undersea-cables-risk-report, caliber.az Tasnim piece May 2026, thediplomat.com May 2026.
cable_incidents.rationale: Multiple credible threat indicators exist (Russian submarine surveillance, Hormuz warnings, repeated Baltic anchor-drag pattern, Matsu minor cut) but no corroborating price/volume signal or official confirmation of a major cable currently unrepaired and causing material connectivity loss; rubric Level 1 (THREATENED) fits — not Level 2 absent clear evidence of a live, major, unrepaired severing.

dissent.view: Medium.com opinion piece (Mar 23 2026) claims 'multiple cables in the Persian Gulf and northern Red Sea routes have gone dark or suffered unexplained damage in the last 72 hours' — unverified, no official corroboration, speculative analysis blog

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: DTCC/FICC readiness survey (published ~late July/early August 2026, per Finadium/Markets Media ~2 weeks prior to 2026-08-10): 79% of GSD Netting Member respondents have required account structures in place; >$1.2T in daily Treasury cash activity already clearing at FICC with $300-400B still to onboard. TBAC Charge Q1Q2 2026 (May 2026, home.treasury.gov) flags 'lack of standardized documentation, uncertainty around sequencing of pre-trade credit check process, required operational builds, and commercial clarity around pricing for done-away activity' as outstanding items; TBAC also notes legal/documentation issues remain a challenge. CME Securities Clearing go-live slipped from Q2 to Q3 2026. Source: DTCC 'Industry Readiness for U.S. Treasury Cash Clearing: A Survey of FICC Membership' (~Aug 2026); TBAC Charge Q1Q2 2026 PDF (home.treasury.gov, May 2026).
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: The DTCC survey shows broad but incomplete readiness — 79% have account structures in place and most are 'actively completing final readiness activities,' which is above the 60% rubric threshold for FRICTION — but TBAC (May 2026) explicitly documents a documentation backlog (non-standardized bilateral agreements), pending done-away model commercial clarity, and CME's CCA go-live delay from Q2 to Q3 2026, all of which map precisely to the rubric's FRICTION criteria of 'documentation backlog' and 'pending exemptive relief.' No deadline extension or operational failure in testing has been reported, precluding a score of 2. dissent.view: DTCC/Brian Steele states 'the industry is well positioned for the Treasury cash clearing deadline on December 31, 2026,' suggesting smooth on-track status closer to rubric score 0.

TBAC/SIFMA (May 2026) warn that the approval of multiple new CCAs (CME, ICE) may be 'challenging for market participants to have the bandwidth for readiness at multiple agencies by the deadline' and that repo clearing bottlenecks 'will not shift without regulatory clarity,' signaling potential score-2 risk for the repo (June 2027) tranche.
